title: Regular domain divisor quotient of canonical strict henselization
statement: Let R be regular, R/(f) regular, and b(f) nonunit at a geometric point. The divisor quotient of the canonical strict henselization is regular and a domain.

source.place: Tag 0EYG (pione-lemma-abhyankar-one-divisor), strict henselization paragraph; Tag 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization); Tag 06LN, regularity under strict henselization.

proof.text: The retained upstream full-colimit theorem pairs the proved regularity and domain components. To recover the original small-colimit formulation, both live consumers use the final-functor coprojection formula to identify the structural maps under smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso. They compose b with this comparison, transport the nonunit hypothesis through its inverse, apply the upstream theorem, and use Ideal.quotientEquiv and IsRegularRing.of_ringEquiv to transfer regularity. The combined quotient consumer also transfers the domain property by MulEquiv.isDomain_iff.

lean.statement:
theorem strictHenselizationRing_regular_divisor_quotient
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsRegularRing R] (f : R)
    [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})]
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (barY : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec R)
    (b : R ⟶ strictHenselization barY)
    (hb : Spec.map b = strictLocalizationToBase barY)
    (hg : ¬ IsUnit (b.hom f)) :
    IsRegularRing (strictHenselization barY ⧸ Ideal.span {b.hom f}) ∧
      IsDomain (strictHenselization barY ⧸ Ideal.span {b.hom f})
